original_question: Describe all the topological types of singularities that may appear in algebraically inte- grable systems with a small (≤ 3) degree of freedom. Next, describe the symplectic invariants of such singularities.
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 2.6 in "Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants".
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target and in fact reproduces Problem 2.6 almost verbatim. It correctly keeps the two-stage task: first classify the topological types of singularities, then describe the symplectic invariants of those singularities. It also correctly retains the restriction to algebraically integrable systems and the low-dimensional bound of at most 3 degrees of freedom.
missing_details: The paper places this problem in the local and semi-global setting: it is about singularities near a singular point or singular fiber, not a global classification of whole systems.
The singularities are those arising from the singular Lagrangian fibration associated with a finite-dimensional integrable system, not arbitrary topological singularities.

The paper explicitly warns that there is no universally accepted definition of algebraic integrability; its intended reading is the paper's 'most natural setting', which should be stated to make the question stand-alone.
In that intended setting, the commuting first integrals F1, ..., Fn are polynomials.

Also in that intended setting, one can naturally complexify the relevant data (phase space, symplectic or Poisson structure, and time) so that the real integrable system becomes the real part of a complex integrable system.
The crucial extra hypothesis on the complexified system is that its general complex fibers are isomorphic to affine parts of Abelian varieties.
The meaning of 'degree of freedom' should be made explicit as n for an n-degree-of-freedom integrable system.

The paper gives a one-degree-of-freedom constraint as context: in that case the Milnor number of a singular point cannot exceed 2. This is not part of the formal problem statement, but it explains why the paper expects the singularities to be highly special.

The refined question should avoid broadening beyond the paper by asking only for singularities that may actually occur under these algebraic-integrability hypotheses, and then only for the symplectic invariants of those same singularities.
refined_question: In the local and semi-global classification of singularities of finite-dimensional integrable systems, determine all topological types of singularities that can occur for algebraically integrable systems with n ≤ 3 degrees of freedom, where algebraic integrability is understood in the paper's most natural sense: the commuting first integrals F1, ..., Fn are polynomials, the phase space together with its symplectic or Poisson structure and time admits a natural complexification, the real system is the real part of a complex integrable system, and the general complex fibers of that complex system are affine parts of Abelian varieties. For each such singularity type, describe its symplectic invariants.
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 2.6 exactly: the wording of your draft matches the official statement almost word for word. The immediately preceding paragraph gives the hidden assumptions needed to make the question self-contained, especially the paper's intended meaning of 'algebraically integrable'. The sentence introducing that paragraph also fixes the scope as local and semi-global. The opening of Section 2 clarifies that the singularities under discussion are singularities of the singular Lagrangian fibration associated with a finite-dimensional integrable system. The paper does not provide an explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 2.6, so no alternate version should be introduced.
